note: Confirmed: Table 7-2 caption (line 123) stated no label convention and no row carried a provenance tag, unlike Table 7-1 and Table 4-2. Recomputed the rows against that convention: 140+24.1=164.1, 140+12.45=152.45, 16x70=1,120, 4x70=280 — all consistent with the stated bytes/param. No column added, so no cell values changed.

Rewrote that sentence (caption, line 267): the axis and every PLOTTED series are aggregate GB; the per-rank 3.1 GB figure is explicitly 'not a plotted series and is not read against the aggregate axis' — it is the 24.9/8 share at 9.5K, read against a single 80 GB rank's HBM, and is stated only to keep the aggregate pool and the per-rank partition visibly separate. Recomputed the MXFP4 sensitivity: (0.98 x 0.53125 + 0.02 x 2) x 70e9 = 39.24375 GB; 640 - 39.24375 - 64 = 536.75625; 536.75625/24.90368 = 21.55 -> 21 — all as printed. Added the missing per-rank test to the same paragraph: per-rank weights 39.24375/8 = 4.906 GB, per-rank KV budget 80 - 4.906 - 8 = 67.09 GB, 67.09/3.11296 = 21.55 -> floor 21 (recomputed). The text now shows the raised ceiling survives the chapter's own binding constraint, and keeps the existing caveat that placement, workspace, fragmentation and SLO are unmeasured.

Not confirmed — recompute refutes the finding. With E2M1 (4-bit) values, 16 values = 8 B and one E4M3 local scale = 1 B, so a 16-value group is 9 B, i.e. 2 groups = 18 B per 32 values = 0.5625 B/value, exactly the rate the chapter prints. 16,777,216 x 0.5625 = 9,437,184 + 4 B global = 9,437,188 B — reproduced exactly. The finding's premise (2 scale bytes per 16 values, giving 20 B per 32) contradicts the chapter's stated 'shares an E4M3 local scale over 16 values'; E4M3 is one byte. P1-087's own evidence text reaches the same conclusion ('the figure is therefore internally consistent'). No edit made; Fig 7.4's rates and the 4096x4096 byte totals stand as printed.
